changes.reason: ACPTCONTRA of category 23071 QAR could not be brought to Acceptances: it fits two rules. Category 23071 QAR carries no ADVICEBL or ACPTBL balance, so on row 48311 it serves only this conflict. Its other leg, ACPTCONTRABL 23071 QAR, is already allocated to Acceptances Liability (row 34367, DKBGL.2680): with the asset leg in ELC the two legs would sit in different sections. The twin rows do not name 23071 (48312 USD, 48983 / 48984 8500000003). Entry 23071 is taken out of L48311; nothing else in the cell changes. Requested by the user on 19 Oct 2026.

findings.title: Remaining-maturity subtraction runs in the wrong direction
findings.detail: Concrete predicate defect if the table represents remaining maturity as indicated by the future maturity headings. System Date - MATURITY.DATE is negative for future maturities, so a future contract can meet both D6 (<=1) and E6 (<=7), while longer positive bands select past-due contracts. A contract maturing 100 days after the as-of date gives -100 and qualifies for both short buckets rather than the >3 to 6 months band. This is a logic illustration, not a value observed in report data.
findings.action: Set a single reporting as-of date and use maturity_date - as_of_date for remaining tenor if that is the regulatory basis. Define the disposition of matured/overdue and same-day contracts separately, and confirm contractual maturity versus any alternative reporting maturity.
findings.limits: Previously documented source-review issue. Exact cell and immutable source hash checked; this is not a new proven balance error.

findings.detail: Concrete predicate defects independent of which balance group is selected. findings.title: Direct credit-quality totals include performing exposures twice and indirect performing total uses the next row
findings.detail: Concrete formula-reference defects relative to the supplied headings, repeated on rows 5, 7-14 and 16-21. F=B+D already totals performing Direct. N=D+F+H+J+L includes performing balances inside Total Non-performing Direct. P=B+D+F+H+J+L counts B and D twice because F=B+D. findings.title: Credit-quality baseline reads movements without an opening balance and changes selected balances by risk
findings.detail: As-of-stock calculation ambiguity. Baseline row 5 explicitly reads DEBIT+CREDIT.MVMT but not OPEN, unlike rows 25/26 which use OPEN+DEBIT+CREDIT. Good/Low Risk selects CURACCOUNT+DUEACCOUNT, Special Mention adds GRCACCOUNT/DELACCOUNT, and nonperforming columns use six ACCOUNT balances, omitting all owner OUTSTANDING deferred-profit components. Risk is therefore controlling both contract classification and selected balance components; amount changes could reflect excluded balances as well as risk classification. A nonzero opening balance with zero movements would contribute zero under the literal movement-only baseline. No numeric source dataset was provided to establish the magnitude.
findings.action: Specify whether this table requires closing outstanding stock or period movements and the exact ECB field/date alignment. For closing stock use an authorized as-of snapshot or correctly aligned opening plus signed movements once. Select the approved table metric separately from the risk-routing predicate so any deliberate risk-specific exclusions remain explicit. Verify OPEN and movement multivalues align to each balance type and reporting currency.
findings.limits: Previously documented source-review issue. Exact cell and immutable source hash checked; this is not a new proven balance error.

findings.detail: As-of-stock calculation ambiguity. Baseline row 5 explicitly reads DEBIT+CREDIT.MVMT but not OPEN, unlike rows 25/26 which use OPEN+DEBIT+CREDIT. Good/Low Risk selects CURACCOUNT+DUEACCOUNT, Special Mention adds GRCACCOUNT/DELACCOUNT, and nonperforming columns use six ACCOUNT balances, omitting all owner OUTSTANDING deferred-profit components. Risk is therefore controlling both contract classification and selected balance components; amount changes could reflect excluded balances as well as risk classification. A nonzero opening balance with zero movements would contribute zero under the literal movement-only baseline. No numeric source dataset was provided to establish the magnitude.
findings.action: Specify whether this table requires closing outstanding stock or period movements and the exact ECB field/date alignment. For closing stock use an authorized as-of snapshot or correctly aligned opening plus signed movements once. Select the approved table metric separately from the risk-routing predicate so any deliberate risk-specific exclusions remain explicit. Verify OPEN and movement multivalues align to each balance type and reporting currency.
findings.limits: Previously documented source-review issue. Exact cell and immutable source hash checked; this is not a new proven balance error.

findings.title: Legacy template is not a flat mapping table
findings.detail: Extract section identity, complete hierarchy and report dimensions before aligning rules. The workbook contains repeated leaf descriptions and varying headers; description-only joins are unsafe.
findings.action: Approve section/row crosswalk to the Temenos source before using legacy logic.
findings.limits: Previously documented source-review issue. Exact cell and immutable source hash checked; this is not a new proven balance error.

findings.title: Ethix loan carrying amount has three metrics
findings.detail: The target must keep OUTSTANDING, AMORTIZED_EARNED, and LOAN_FEES separate and compose the approved carrying amount. User-provided T24 groups cover the first two; no T24 fee group has been supplied.
findings.action: Supply the bank-specific T24 source and balance types for LOAN_FEES, fee sign, valuation basis and whether already embedded in another group.
findings.limits: Previously documented source-review issue. Exact cell and immutable source hash checked; this is not a new proven balance error.

findings.title: Loan sector and government exceptions are legacy filters
findings.detail: These are Ethix client/product classifications, not T24 balance types. Resident/nonresident variants are asymmetrical in the legacy text.
findings.action: Approve Ethix-to-T24 field dictionaries for SIC, RIM, personal status and residency, and resolve the K37/L37 RIM2398 asymmetry.
findings.limits: Previously documented source-review issue. Exact cell and immutable source hash checked; this is not a new proven balance error.

findings.title: Private-sector SYN and Islamic rules can overlap
findings.detail: A SYN loan with nonpersonal SIC4 may satisfy both main private-sector rules. Copying the text without a precedence/partition rule can double count; K41 also mixes loan-file and GL populations.
findings.action: Approve mutually exclusive private-sector finance/product rules, SYN sector restrictions, the GL1300050001 allocation and inside/outside amount symmetry.

findings.title: Ethix product classification codes are not T24 equivalents
findings.detail: These selectors inform an approved product crosswalk. They do not establish universal T24 categories or ECB balance types.
findings.action: Approve bank-specific product/category mapping, especially Murabaha category3713 and its CLM subset.

findings.title: Credit risk, maturity and personal subdivisions require external feeds
findings.detail: Required reporting dimensions cannot all be inferred from balance types. Missing risk/BO sources must remain explicit exceptions, not default assignments.
findings.action: Approve risk/BO feed schemas, as-of dates, joins, classification fields and reconciliation controls.

findings.title: Deferred income currently uses legacy GL selection
findings.detail: Do not automatically equate these GL selectors or every deferred-income report row with the user UNEARNED_PROFIT group without an approved crosswalk. Principal/deferred-state and risk dimensions still require validation.
findings.action: Approve replacement of legacy GL2300 rule with the appropriate loan population and T24 deferred-profit groups, including signs and performing status.
